examples.input: Julius Caesar checked the latest battle reports on WhatsApp before crossing the Rubicon.
Julius Caesar received handwritten battle reports from his couriers before crossing the Rubicon.
Queen Victoria streamed her Diamond Jubilee celebration live on Instagram Stories.
Queen Victoria had her Diamond Jubilee celebration photographed and reported in Victorian newspapers.
Leonardo da Vinci regularly saved backups of his Mona Lisa sketches to cloud storage.
Leonardo da Vinci kept his preliminary Mona Lisa sketches organized in leather bound notebooks.
George Washington sent encrypted emails to his generals during the winter at Valley Forge.
George Washington sent sealed handwritten letters to his generals during the winter at Valley Forge.
Marie Antoinette used the Uber Eats app to have pastries delivered to her chambers in Versailles.
Marie Antoinette summoned palace servants to bring freshly baked pastries to her chambers in Versailles.
Genghis Khan relied on GPS navigation to plot the fastest route across the Eurasian steppe.
Genghis Khan relied on experienced scouts to plot the fastest route across the Eurasian steppe.
Abraham Lincoln hosted a Zoom call with his cabinet to draft the Emancipation Proclamation.
Abraham Lincoln met face to face with his cabinet to draft the Emancipation Proclamation.
Socrates recorded a weekly philosophy podcast that was downloaded throughout Athens.
Socrates engaged in spoken philosophical dialogues with citizens throughout Athens.
During his exile, Napoleon binge watched historical dramas on Netflix to pass the time on Saint Helena.
During his exile, Napoleon passed the time on Saint Helena by dictating his memoirs and reading books.
Cleopatra posted a series of selfies with Mark Antony to her Facebook timeline.
Cleopatra sent papyrus letters to Mark Antony carried by river boats along the Nile.
Julius Caesar commended the Ming dynasty artillery generals on their innovative use of gunpowder cannons during the Siege of Nanjing.
Julius Caesar commended his Roman engineers on their innovative use of ballistae during the Siege of Alesia.
In a series of late-night emails, Isaac Newton thanked Albert Einstein for clarifying the finer points of general relativity.
In a series of letters, Isaac Newton debated Robert Hooke about the nature of light and color.
Pharaoh Ramses II scheduled a video conference with Alexander the Great to coordinate their campaigns against Persia.
Pharaoh Ramses II ordered his generals to secure the Syrian frontier before launching the campaign at Kadesh.
Queen Elizabeth I summoned Marie Curie to Whitehall Palace to demonstrate the glowing properties of radium.
Queen Elizabeth I summoned her advisor John Dee to Whitehall Palace to discuss navigational routes to the New World.
Chief Sitting Bull phoned President Franklin D. Roosevelt to express concerns about how the New Deal would affect the Lakota people.
Chief Sitting Bull met with U.S. Army officers at Fort Buford to discuss the terms of his surrender.
Leonardo da Vinci saved his sketches to a cloud drive on his iPad Pro while designing the aerial screw.
Leonardo da Vinci filled pages of his codices with quill-and-ink sketches of the aerial screw.
George Washington posted a story on TikTok announcing he would not seek a third term as president.
George Washington announced his decision not to seek a third term through his Farewell Address, which was printed in American newspapers.
During a particularly long evening at Versailles, Marie Antoinette relaxed by streaming a season of reality television on her flat-screen.
During long evenings at Versailles, Marie Antoinette often passed the time by attending private musical performances and playing cards.
In 1776, Benjamin Franklin advised smallpox patients to get vaccinated with the mRNA-based vaccine he had helped develop.
In 1776, Benjamin Franklin encouraged the public to undergo smallpox variolation, a preventive practice he strongly supported.
During the Crimean War in 1855, Florence Nightingale ordered CT scans of injured soldiers to precisely locate internal bleeding.
During the Crimean War in 1855, Florence Nightingale compiled detailed statistics on soldier mortality to identify preventable causes of death.
